newsitem.title: CHINA: China hits at illegal stock trade, sacks bank head.
newsitem.headline: China hits at illegal stock trade, sacks bank head.

text.p: China's regulators cracked down on Thursday on a blue chip bank, sacking its president for illegal stock trading, and punished three top brokerages for share speculation and misconduct.

The latest crackdown on China's volatile stock markets came just a week after regulators ordered state banks to stop trading on the stock markets and wind up their positions in 10 days as part of a drive to cool market speculation.

The central bank, the People's Bank of China, and top regulators issued a notice punishing the leading blue chip on the Shenzhen stock market, the Shenzhen Development Bank, and sacking the heads of three of China's premier brokerage houses for speculation and illegal trading.

The move against the Shenzhen Development Bank, China's only domestically listed bank and heavily weighted on the Shenzhen index, had been expected since the bank this year announced it was investigating share trading malpractices involving its own stock.
Bank chairman He Yun was sacked and all bank earnings from trading in its own shares were confiscated.

The central bank notice confirmed the removal of Guangshen Railway Co Ltd's chairman and accountant after it improperly used part of a 300 million yuan investment for share trading. It ordered the removal of the president of China's largest brokerage, Shenyin & Wanguo, as well as the heads of two other leading houses, Haitong Securities and China Everbright Securities, for illegally obtaining funds from banks to trade.

The securities firms used the funds to speculate in stocks, including Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development Co Ltd, Shanghai Petrochemical Co Ltd and Shenzhen Nanyou Property Development Co Ltd, it said.
The notice announced disciplinary action against the head of the Shanghai branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China for extending loans to securities houses to trade on the stock markets.

"Financial and securities regulators stressed that, in the future, they will further intensify implementation of the law," said a People's Daily commentary, issued by the official Xinhua news agency and to be carried in the newspaper on Friday.

"Not only will violators of laws and regulations be given administrative punishment but we will also pursue criminal responsibility in accordance with the law," thundered the mouthpiece of the Communist Party.
"This demonstrates the state's resolute determination to protect the normal order of the markets and to protect the legal rights and interests of investors," the commentary said.
A similar commentary last December sent China's two stock markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen into a nosedive.
"If there is a law we will act according to the law, if there are violations of the law we will pursue the violations, we will strictly implement the law," it said.
"To maintain the openness and fairness of the securities market and to ensure healthy development of the securities market, we must further strengthen market supervision.
"Our securities market is still not mature and checking excessive speculation is a long term and difficult mission."
The latest crackdown was announced after China's stock markets closed.
Sentiment had been weak in slow trade, with foreign currency B shares ending slightly higher and domestic A shares falling.
